previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of recurrent left lower extremity cellulitis, chronic venous stasis, lipodermatosclerosis, bioprosthetic aortic valve, pacemaker, and heart failure was admitted for worsening left leg pain, erythema, and swelling unresponsive to outpatient oral antibiotics. She presented with a low-grade fever and a history of recent watery diarrhea. In the ED, she received IV vancomycin and ceftriaxone, and imaging ruled out DVT but confirmed significant subcutaneous edema. During her hospital stay, she improved clinically with IV antibiotics, and a PICC line was placed for outpatient continuation of vancomycin. Her acute kidney injury, attributed to volume depletion while on torsemide, resolved with IV fluids, and the diuretic was held at discharge. She was discharged home with instructions to complete a 10-day IV antibiotic course, hold torsemide and potassium until follow-up, and monitor for recurrence of infection.

Brief Hospital Course:
=============================
BRIEF SUMMARY 
=============================

___ w/ bioprosthetic AVR, PPM, PAF, DVT on warfarin, with 
lipodermatosclerosis and chronic venous stasis dermatitis, 
admitted with acute on recurrent LLE cellulitis but antibiotics 
were soon discontinued when it was felt the most likely 
presentation was consistent with CVI changes. This is in the 
setting of a c diff infection that was recently diagnosed as an 
outpatient. We consulted dermatology who recommended aggressive 
wound care with topical steroids. 

==============================
PROBLEM BASED SUMMARY 
==============================

#Acute on chronic lipodermatosclerosis/stasis dermatitis
This patient has a PMHx of chronic venous stasis, obesity, and 
lower extremity edema, with history of recurrent lower extremity 
cellulitis over past ___ years, and is followed by ID and 
Dermatology. She recently completed a 10d course of IV vanc (LD: 
___ then trialed on PCN ppx but was interrupted d/t C. 
diff for which she was
started on PO vanc 5d PTA. In the ED here, the patient received 
IV Vanc and was given bolus NS 500mL. On admission, she was not 
in distress, with symptoms similar to prior hospitalizations and 
reassuring labs (no leukocytosis, Chem7 WNL). On exam, she was
afebrile with stable vital signs. She has underlying venous 
stasis changes on both legs, with LLE findings concerning for 
cellulitis especially given spread of erythema to the foot which 
is a recent change over the last few days. RLE more concerning 
for CVI changes or exacerbation. After further evaluation and 
discussion with ID and dermatology, it was decided to 
discontinue the IV vancomycin given that her current clinical 
state did not seem infectious and that the lower extremity 
symptoms were likely due to her chronic venous insufficiency and 
lipodermatosclerosis/stasis dermatitis due to this CVI. Upon 
discharge she will have a ___ help with daily dressings to 
bilateral lower extremities given new recommendations by 
dermatology that also included a topical steroid. 

#C. diff colitis
Pt has had multiple episodes of diarrhea since ___. Pt had 
recently finished a course of abx for cellulitis and was seen by 
her ID specialist on ___ w/ c/f an infectious process as the 
cause of her diarrhea. Stool samples were taken and pt was wound 
to have a positive C. diff sample. Pt was empirically started on 
PO vancomycin on ___ and will continue the full 2 week 
course (___)

#Mild low PO intake
Patient reports low PO intake over past week+ with low UOP at 
home. She was dry on exam with extremely dry mucous membranes. 
Her electrolytes were stable. Her BUN was slightly elevated at 
32 and her Cr at 1.2(baseline 0.9-1.1). The most likely etiology 
is ongoing diarrhea from C. diff infection with low appetite and 
nausea and self-reported low water intake. She is also on 
Torsemide 40 mg at home, so could consider slight overdiuresis. 
While in house we reduced her on torsemide 20mg and replenished 
fluids as necessary.

# Chronic pain: We continued her home oxycontin bid and 
oxycodone 5mg TID for breakthrough pain

# CHF - We continued her home torsemide 20mg, no ___ continue 
home metop 50mg daily. 

# pAFib - There were no exacerbations, we continued warfarin and 
metoprolol (fractionated to tartrate 12.5 mg q6h while in 
house). We checked her INR as well and it was within normal 
limits. 

# Severe AS s/p AVR c/b bradycardic arrest s/p PPM- We continued 
her torsemide 20mg home med 

# Eczema - Clobetasol ointment was restarted on bilateral lower 
extremities as a recommendation from dermatology.

# B12def / Anemia - at baseline.

# GERD - continued home PPI

# HL - continued home statin

# Chronic pancreatitis - continued creon 

# RLSS - home parmipexole continued

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to ___ 
swelling, redness, and pain to both lower extremities. We were 
concerned for an infection to be the cause of your symptoms and 
started you on IV antibiotics for precautionary purposes. After 
further evaluation and a discussion with infectious disease and 
dermatology, we concluded that the cause of  your symptoms were 
unlikely to be caused by an infection but rather a build up of 
excess fluid and a dermatologic reaction due to that excess 
fluid. We changed the protocol for the wound care to both of 
your lower extremities and your symptoms of swelling, redness, 
and pain improved. 

You also had an infection of your intestines prior to admission 
known as C. diff colitis. You were given antibiotics for this 
infection and fluids through your IV for rehydration. Your 
symptoms including diarrhea improved.

Please continue your course of oral vancomycin and wound 
dressing changes daily as instructed. If your condition does not 
improve or your symptoms become worse, please contact your 
primary care physician or present to the emergency department.

Thank you for allowing us to be a part of your care,

Your ___ Team
